---
title: "Federal Procurement: computer hardware"
subtitle: "What every US federal agency promised to spend on computers, servers, storage and data centre equipment, by month"
---

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site

init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

monthly, meta = site.load("procurement", "monthly")
groups, groups_meta = site.load("procurement", "by_group")
agencies, agencies_meta = site.load("procurement", "agencies")
check, check_meta = site.load("procurement", "totals_check")
finding = meta.get("finding")


def fy_label(year, provisional):
    return f"{int(year)}*" if provisional else str(int(year))
```

The US government publishes every contract it signs. This page adds up the contracts for
computer hardware: what each agency promised to pay in each month, from October 2016. The
figures are obligations, which is money promised when a contract or an order is signed. Money
actually paid is a different figure and has [its own page](paid.qmd).
[Who the suppliers are](suppliers.qmd) is a third.

## Value by month

```{python}
#| output: asis
if monthly.empty:
    print(site.empty_state(meta, "Monthly value"))
else:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
    m = monthly.assign(period=pd.to_datetime(monthly["period"]))
    firm = m[~m["provisional"]]
    last = firm.iloc[-1]
    year_ago = firm[firm["period"] == last["period"] - pd.DateOffset(years=1)]
    line = (f'{site.finding_badge(finding)} In the twelve months to '
            f'{last["period"]:%B %Y}, agencies obligated '
            f'${last["obligations_12m"] / 1e9:.2f} billion for computer hardware')
    if not year_ago.empty and pd.notna(year_ago.iloc[0]["obligations_12m"]):
        before = year_ago.iloc[0]["obligations_12m"]
        change = 100 * (last["obligations_12m"] / before - 1)
        line += (f', {"up" if change >= 0 else "down"} {abs(change):.1f}% on the twelve months '
                 f'before (${before / 1e9:.2f} billion)')
    print(line + ". Later months are provisional and are left out of that figure.\n")
```

```{python}
if not monthly.empty:
    m = monthly.assign(period=pd.to_datetime(monthly["period"]),
                       bn=monthly["obligations"] / 1e9)
    m["Status"] = m["provisional"].map({True: "Provisional (defence records still arriving)",
                                        False: "Reported"})
    fig = px.bar(m, x="period", y="bn", color="Status",
                 color_discrete_map={"Reported": "#2a6f97",
                                     "Provisional (defence records still arriving)": "#b8c4cc"},
                 labels={"bn": "Net obligations, $ billion", "period": ""})
    fig.add_vline(x=pd.Timestamp(meta["code_change"] + "-01"), line_dash="dot",
                  line_color="#666")
    fig.add_annotation(x=pd.Timestamp(meta["code_change"] + "-01"), y=1, yref="paper",
                       text="Product codes rewritten", showarrow=False, xanchor="left",
                       font=dict(size=11, color="#666"))
    fig.update_layout(height=420, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10),
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.15, title=""))
    fig.show()
```

The tall bar every September is the end of the fiscal year, when agencies commit what is left
of their budgets. The dotted line is 1 October 2020, when the government replaced its list of
product codes. Spending before and after the line is not on the same footing; see the limits
at the foot of the page.

## What kind of hardware

```{python}
if groups.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(groups_meta, "Kinds of hardware")))
else:
    g = groups.assign(bn=groups["obligations"] / 1e9,
                      year=[fy_label(y, p) for y, p in zip(groups["fiscal_year"],
                                                           groups["provisional"])])
    fig = px.bar(g, x="year", y="bn", color="group",
                 labels={"bn": "Net obligations, $ billion", "year": "Fiscal year", "group": ""})
    fig.update_layout(height=420, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10),
                      legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.2))
    fig.show()
```

## Which agencies buy

```{python}
if agencies.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(agencies_meta, "Agencies")))
else:
    a = agencies[agencies["obligations"].abs() >= 1e6]
    t = a.assign(obligations=a["obligations"] / 1e6,
                 fiscal_year=[fy_label(y, p) for y, p in zip(a["fiscal_year"],
                                                             a["provisional"])])[
        ["fiscal_year", "agency", "obligations", "share_pct"]
    ].rename(columns={"fiscal_year": "Fiscal year", "agency": "Agency",
                      "obligations": "Net obligations, $m",
                      "share_pct": "Share of the year, %"}).round(1)
    show(t, paging=True, pageLength=15, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```

## Do these figures match USAspending's own?

The rule was written before the figures were computed: for every month, the transactions
downloaded for this page must add up to within 1% of the monthly figure USAspending's own
search gives for the same filters.

```{python}
#| output: asis
if check.empty:
    print(site.empty_state(check_meta, "Totals check"))
else:
    ok = check_meta["criterion_met"]
    n, good = check_meta["months"], check_meta["months_within_limit"]
    gap = 100 * (check_meta["published_total"] / check_meta["ours_total"] - 1)
    if ok:
        print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**Yes.** All {n} months are within '
              f'{check_meta["tolerance_pct"]:.0f}% of USAspending\'s figure; the worst is '
              f'{check_meta["worst_month_gap_pct"]:.2f}%.\n:::\n')
    else:
        print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**No. The criterion is not met.** {good} of {n} months are '
              f'within {check_meta["tolerance_pct"]:.0f}% of USAspending\'s figure and '
              f'{n - good} are not; the worst month is {check_meta["worst_month_gap_pct"]:.1f}% '
              f'away. Over the whole period USAspending\'s search figure is '
              f'{abs(gap):.1f}% {"higher" if gap > 0 else "lower"} than the sum of the '
              f'transactions it lets anyone download. The limit has not been moved.\n:::\n')
    print(site.finding_line(check_meta.get("finding")))
```

### Where the difference comes from

The rule above failed, so every month outside the limit was checked again, one transaction at
a time: the transactions behind USAspending's search figure were listed and matched with the
download on award, modification, date and amount. This second check was added after the first
failed, and it [is recorded as a new test](../failures.qmd).

```{python}
#| output: asis
rec = check_meta.get("reconciliation") or []
if rec:
    ok_rows = [d for d in rec if "extra_copies" in d]
    copies = sum(d["extra_copies"] for d in ok_rows)
    copies_sum = sum(d["extra_copies_sum"] for d in ok_rows)
    missing = sum(d["search_rows_not_in_download"] for d in ok_rows)
    unchecked = len(rec) - len(ok_rows)
    done = sum(d["reconciled"] for d in rec)
    worst = max([d["gap_after_copies_share"] for d in ok_rows] or [0])
    if check_meta.get("all_missed_months_reconciled"):
        print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**The download is complete; the search figure counts some '
              f'transactions twice.** In all {len(rec)} months outside the limit, every '
              f'transaction the search lists is also in the download. The search lists '
              f'{copies:,} transactions a second time, worth ${copies_sum / 1e6:,.1f} million '
              f'together. With those second copies removed, the search and the download agree '
              f'to within {100 * worst:.3f}% in every one of these months. The figures on this '
              f'page are the download, with each transaction counted once.\n:::\n')
    else:
        print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**Not fully explained.** {done} of {len(rec)} months outside '
              f'the limit reconcile row by row; {unchecked} could not be listed this time and '
              f'{missing:,} transactions the search lists are not in the download. Until every '
              f'month reconciles, treat the monthly figures as approximate.\n:::\n')
    print(site.finding_line(check_meta.get("reconcile_finding")))
```

```{python}
rec = [d for d in check_meta.get("reconciliation") or [] if "extra_copies" in d]
if rec:
    t = pd.DataFrame(rec)
    t = t.assign(download=t["download"] / 1e6, search=t["search"] / 1e6,
                 extra_copies_sum=t["extra_copies_sum"] / 1e6,
                 gap=100 * t["gap_after_copies_share"])[
        ["period", "download", "search", "extra_copies", "extra_copies_sum",
         "search_rows_not_in_download", "gap", "reconciled"]
    ].rename(columns={"period": "Month", "download": "Download, $m",
                      "search": "Search figure, $m", "extra_copies": "Second copies in search",
                      "extra_copies_sum": "Value of second copies, $m",
                      "search_rows_not_in_download": "Search rows missing from download",
                      "gap": "Gap left, %", "reconciled": "Reconciled"}).round(3)
    show(t, paging=True, pageLength=10, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```

```{python}
if not check.empty:
    c = check.assign(period=pd.to_datetime(check["period"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m"),
                     ours=check["ours"] / 1e6, published=check["published"] / 1e6)[
        ["period", "ours", "published", "gap_pct", "within_limit"]
    ].rename(columns={"period": "Month", "ours": "Download, $m",
                      "published": "USAspending search, $m", "gap_pct": "Gap, %",
                      "within_limit": "Within 1%"}).round(2)
    show(c.iloc[::-1], paging=True, pageLength=12, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```
